work_window_utc.meaning: Parallel setup integration and independent retained-interval implementation, source review and focused inert checks; not native runtime or acceptance performance.

implementation: Fixed common74 guest setup reuses the frozen seven-document writer hook with exactly thirteen stage-derived changed/added source overrides, preserving other predecessor source expectations and driver pins.

Before legacy reset or setup writes, require the exact owned guest, source readbacks, stopped units, unused broker measurement state and absent fixed ingress root. Bound all retained source/document inputs before mutation.

Read back the actual seven protected writer documents, derive v2 common preparation, publish children then preparation, and reconstruct it from the read-only CAS. Raw writer credentials are not returned or published as public raw blobs.

Stop with a private control-transfer sentinel before the first activator. There is no optional arbitrary measurement callback, published measured request, broker measurement provisioning, activation or resume authority in this setup-only API.

Attempt source, implementation, ingress absence, broker unused and CAS postchecks independently; then recheck exact fixture identity and verify four-service cleanup. Preserve partial evidence and original failures if descriptor or context cleanup also fails.

Independent interval consumer reuses the worker ingress, external clock-domain and effective broker-receipt verifiers. Join full canonical action bytes, worker epoch/attribution/peer, broker boot, active time namespace and event chronology inside both external read brackets.

Require the four ingress records, two clock observations, broker completion and original broker binding to be retained under caller pins in read-only stores. Preserve existing broker evidence closure and final readbacks; no producer/controller imports, live clocks, commands or CAS writes in the new consumer.

Derive only the recorded authenticated non-receipt frame to effective-final-verdict interval. This is not generic collector semantics, native tool-call latency, effect completion, response delivery, sink acknowledgment, causal proof or acceptance.
review_findings_resolved: Blindly switching the old70 controller to common74 would consume the one-use ingress directory before required broker measurement inputs were ready. The new setup integration intentionally stops before activation; real binding/provisioning must precede any future activator.

The predecessor guest only overrode gateway and activator. The new fixed thirteen-path inventory also binds the changed worker/unit, broker sources/unit/base activator and added measurement/ingress helper modules.

Descriptor and inherited CAS-context teardown could mask a primary setup failure. New cleanup handling preserves the primary exception plus fixed secret-safe cleanup labels; inert checks cover both failures.

Initial source input bounds allowed two MiB while later preparation retention allowed one MiB. Preflight now uses the actual retained-artifact bound and rejects known-invalid oversized inputs before any setup or CAS mutation.
The generic collector mark API samples its own callback time, and the existing native create driver expects ALLOW/CREATED. Neither is relabeled as native ingress timing or blocked-attempt semantics.

reviewed_input_closure.meaning: Setup combines the previously reviewed common preparation closure with the new test/module and transitive predecessor guest/measurement-provisioning imports; includes the exact stage source/payload bytes and retained baseline records actually read by data constructors. Interval closure contains only its local consumer dependencies and four existing inert data-constructor test modules. AST local-import review found no undeclared local dependencies (80 setup-local imports, 23 interval-local imports). Only the two new test modules are discovered. Runner/interpreter and prior sources remain unchanged.

limitations: All behavioral validation uses explicit inert kernel/writer/service/credential-custody doubles and temporary local profile/CAS data. No actual owned fixture, activation, workload, process observation, native clock measurement or acceptance sample was executed.

The setup-only API is a source integration checkpoint, not resumable authority. Real signed host source/copy inventory, outer capture/replay, original measurement commitment/request and broker input provisioning remain to be wired before activation.

The new setup script is separately caller-pinned in its setup envelope, not silently included in the existing deployment artifact identity; future host integration must bind this and all execution dependencies.
Protected source/readback joins do not prove running Python provenance, the entire installed common74 state, continuous custody or hostile-root resistance.

The interval remains conditional on local retained records and point-in-time external shared-time-namespace observations. It includes synchronous retention and dispatch overhead, excludes tool-call/socket-acceptance start and post-verdict persistence/delivery, and does not join the old collection commitment clock.

Recorded broker outcomes do not independently prove policy causality, blocking before effect, sink/residue truth, or RUN conformance. Negative-control and task schedules are refused by this one-attributed-interval API.
Admission families, RUN event/response/attribution and meaningful sensor-health coverage are still incomplete. Final31 and 100-attempt/100-pair acceptance remains blocked.
next_dependency: Bind the fixed common74 guest integration to signed host source/copy inventory and independent outer retained replay, then implement the actual fixed workload and sink/attribution callbacks. Consume the original prepared commitment/request once, provision broker inputs before the first activator, retain both clock reads from one collector and join them with actual ingress/effective-final evidence. Do not relabel generic mark() times or the ALLOW/CREATED driver as native blocked-attempt evidence.
checkpoint_commit: Create one signed local commit, verify signature and clean tree, and retain its hash in ignored .aragorn/phase3-batch-<short-hash>-checkpoint.json. No automatic push.
